action: Place the probe in the transverse orientation just above the pubic bone. Aim the beam deep into the pelvis.
interpretation: Identify the bladder as the first anatomical landmark.

action: Confidently identify the bladder above the vaginal stripe. Tilt the top of the transducer towards the feet.
interpretation: Visualize the uterus coming into view and ideally identify a fetus within it.

action: Prepare to perform the crown-rump length (CRL) measurement.
interpretation: Establish this as the easiest measurement for first trimester gestational age.

action: Maneuver the probe to elongate the fetal view.
interpretation: Obtain the maximal pole of the crown-rump distance.

action: Fan the probe around and rotate. Adjust until confident the maximal length is captured.
interpretation: Identify the true longitudinal axis of the fetus.

action: Quickly freeze the scan. Cine ('sinney') back through the frames.
interpretation: Locate the specific frame that demonstrates the best pole for measurement.

action: Activate calipers for CRL. Place one caliper pixel at the top (crown) and one pixel at the bottom (rump).
interpretation: Calculate the estimated gestational age (e.g., 12 weeks, 2 days).
